title: Fats Waller's easygoing leadership; "The Fats Waller" at the Apollo
summary: Thomas describes Waller as definite without forcing his ideas, mentions the later Jitterbug Waltz recording, and recalls the Apollo rehearsal where Fats wanted to be introduced as "the Fats Waller".

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: OK. Joe Thomas, tape 4, where he's continuing the story about Fats Waller.
You mean the great Thomas "Fats" Waller?

Well, he's a tremendous musician and we had gotten through gigs but the gig that impressed me the most about Fats' personality was the gig at Atlantic City. And, I was worried about his musicianship and all because he was a very (sweet) musician. He's one of the most definite people I've ever worked around without forcing his impression on you. He gave you the idea you are on your own, which you are, really, too. Tremendous person. At that time he came to town through some sequence of events -- I don't know how it happened -- xxxxxxxxxxxx he found out what I was doing. And, incidentally, I'm jumping ahead of the story recording setyp. I made this last recording with him, "the Jitterbug Waltz," you know.
Sure, sure. So, anyhow, you know he's is a beautiful guy.

So now going to the theater after you get off the bus we're riding these miles ... you got the principals, you got the chorus girls, you know, that's the show in those days. They're all lined up. You get those things with dancing and Tom Whaley's directing, you know, and everybody is trying to get together. This all happens after we go somewhere to get ourselves cleaned up because the Apollo Theater down in that basement has got to be smelly and everybody is ...
I thought we were in Atlantic City.
Yeah but we haven't gotten there yet.
Oh, I see. You're rehearsing in the Apollo here.
And everybody would be smelly together and that must be terrible (?)
Yeah, well, that was a dirty hole.

Or it was at that time. So, what happened was we got this thing together so Fats isn't here. So they're running down the principals, the stars of the show ... now, ladies and gentlemen, the great xx Thomas "Fats" Waller. He said, No, baby, sock (?) it cool. The Fats Fats Waller, you dig it?
